explainedBy: Stevens stands stiffly in the bare study facing the estate's new American owner, Mr. Faraday.

storyboard.claim: Lord Darlington has died, the estate is sold, and Stevens must serve its new American buyer.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens in upright formal tails standing rigid before Faraday, who relaxes casually in the empty study.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the 1956 post-war era, moving from aristocratic English diplomacy to American ownership.
storyboard.addedInformation: Directly contrasts Stevens' stiff aristocratic posture with Faraday's relaxed informal demeanor.

explainedBy: Faraday lounges casually on the chaise longue, introducing an easygoing informality that disorients Stevens.

storyboard.claim: Faraday's casual posture and relaxed manners completely upend the rigid British hierarchy Stevens revere.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Faraday stretched out comfortably smiling while Stevens remains rigidly erect beside him, deeply uncomfortable.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the study confrontation, focusing on the cultural gulf between the two men.
storyboard.addedInformation: Highlights the cultural clash between American informality and British butler protocol.

explainedBy: Faraday urges Stevens to take a motoring holiday, offering generously to pay for all travel expenses.

storyboard.claim: Faraday tells Stevens to take a vacation and promises to cover the motoring fuel expenses himself.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Faraday gestures warmly toward Stevens, offering paid time off that leaves Stevens visibly uneasy.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Develops Faraday's proposal that sets the book's motoring journey in motion.
storyboard.addedInformation: Captures the bizarre irony of an employer urging an employee to take leisure at his expense.

explainedBy: Stevens realizes the tragic irony of spending decades confined to great houses serving masters without ever seeing the world.

storyboard.claim: Stevens' total professional confinement kept him from ever experiencing the world outside Darlington Hall.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens standing alone in somber reflection in the quiet hall, looking inward with solemn regret.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reflects on Faraday's piercing question about servants never seeing their own country.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the psychological cost of lifelong institutional isolation behind grand estate walls.

explainedBy: The aristocratic social order Stevens sacrificed his youth and soul to uphold is sold off to commercial buyers.

storyboard.claim: The entire noble tradition Stevens surrendered his personal life for is ultimately auctioned to the highest bidder.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens slumped in sorrow beside the gold coin icon, symbolizing the commercial auction of Darlington Hall.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the critique of institutional loyalty to its inevitable economic end.
storyboard.addedInformation: Visualizes the commercial sale of noble prestige with the coin icon and Stevens' slumped defeat.

explainedBy: Stevens mourns his vanished aristocratic order while awkwardly fumbling to respond to Faraday's jokes.

storyboard.claim: The buyer does not understand aristocratic codes, forcing Stevens to fumble awkwardly with American joking.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens attempting a stiff, unnatural conversational smile while Faraday chuckles easily.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transitions from historical decline to Stevens' immediate interpersonal struggle with his new employer.
storyboard.addedInformation: Contrasts Faraday's easy wit with Stevens' strained, anxious effort to simulate humor.

callout.text: DOES NOT KNOW HOW TO RESPOND

explainedBy: Stevens is deeply unsettled by an employer who cracks jokes and demands that the estate run with only four staff.

storyboard.claim: Stevens cannot navigate informal bantering or the collapse of the estate's domestic staff.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens pacing thoughtfully, agonizing over how to maintain butler decorum under drastically reduced conditions.
storyboard.onScreenText: DOES NOT KNOW HOW TO RESPOND
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Deepens Stevens' bewilderment over both personal conversational banter and structural downsizing.
storyboard.addedInformation: Emphasizes Stevens' internal paralysis when confronted with informal expectations.

explainedBy: A flow diagram contrasting Darlington Hall's historic glory of 28 servants with Faraday's skeletal crew of four.

storyboard.claim: Stevens spent his life orchestrating 28 servants, but now must justify his role with only four staff.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow diagram illustrating the severe collapse in domestic staff from twenty-eight servants down to four.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Provides concrete historical scale to Stevens' domestic staff crisis.
storyboard.addedInformation: Quantifies the collapse of aristocratic manor operations into a commercialized skeleton team.

explainedBy: Stevens defensively rationalizes taking on menial domestic duties as broad-minded professional flexibility.

storyboard.claim: Stevens rationalizes taking on diminished domestic chores as broad-minded professional duty.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens speaking with formal composure, insisting that domestic compromises reflect noble adaptability.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows how Stevens rationalizes his loss of prestige to preserve his dignity.
storyboard.addedInformation: Illustrates Stevens' psychological defense of recasting diminished status as virtuous flexibility.

explainedBy: The host questions Stevens' misery by noting that Faraday is being a generous boss who pays for his travel expenses.

storyboard.claim: Faraday acts with genuine generosity by acknowledging Stevens' hard work and offering fully funded travel.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Faraday speaking warmly with an open posture while Stevens listens with tense, guarded suspicion.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the counter-perspective challenging Stevens' chronic misery.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sharpens the paradox: Stevens treats kindness and generosity as unsettling threats.

explainedBy: Stevens experiences genuine personal freedom as terrifying because he has fully institutionalized himself.

storyboard.claim: Personal autonomy is terrifying to someone whose entire identity depends on total institutional servitude.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens gripping his lapels with an anxious, unsettled look as the concept of unstructured freedom threatens him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Unpacks the psychological reason why Faraday's benevolent offer paralyzes Stevens with anxiety.
storyboard.addedInformation: Identifies institutionalization as the core reason Stevens dreads personal freedom.

explainedBy: If service is merely an ordinary commercial job, then Stevens' sacrifice of his dying father was entirely pointless.

storyboard.claim: If butlering is merely an ordinary commercial job, then ignoring his dying father was an unforgivable waste.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens bowed in painful contemplation, horrified by the looming revelation that his supreme sacrifice was meaningless.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Begins a rapid cascade of retrospective sacrifices rendered absurd by modern reality.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strikes through the justification of duty, revealing the tragic cost of neglecting his father.

explainedBy: Firing Jewish housemaids and abandoning Miss Kenton are exposed as horrifying, pointless sacrifices.

storyboard.claim: Lord Darlington's casual demise exposes Stevens' moral compromises and romantic sacrifices as entirely in vain.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A tight framing of Stevens' pale, despondent face as decades of repressed grief and guilt overwhelm him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reaches the emotional climax of the sacrifice sequence: total existential nullification.
storyboard.addedInformation: Framed in closeUp to expose the devastating realization of a squandered moral life.

explainedBy: With professional duty shattered, Stevens' hollowed soul is left completely destitute with nothing to hold onto.

storyboard.claim: When the artificial fortress of professional dignity collapses, the individual is left completely hollow.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens standing slumped and defeated in the empty room, stripped of all aristocratic delusions.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Concludes the Darlington Hall transition, delivering the book toward its ultimate romantic reckoning.
storyboard.addedInformation: Visualizes the complete psychological destitution of an emotional ascetic.

explainedBy: Stevens and Miss Kenton sit together in the rain at a bus stop in Little Compton after twenty years apart.

storyboard.claim: After twenty years of estrangement, Stevens and Miss Kenton sit together at a rain-swept bus station.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens and Miss Kenton sitting side by side in subdued overcoats under the dreary coastal rain.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transports the narrative to the climactic meeting in Little Compton.
storyboard.addedInformation: Establishes the somber, rain-swept physical reunion of the two separated protagonists.

explainedBy: Miss Kenton confesses she often wonders what life with Stevens might have been, breaking his heart in silence.

storyboard.claim: Miss Kenton confesses that she sometimes imagines the happy life she and Stevens might have shared.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Miss Kenton speaking quietly with tears in her eyes as Stevens sits motionless beside the breaking heart motif.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Advances the bus stop sequence to Kenton's momentous admission of reciprocal love.
storyboard.addedInformation: Directly links Miss Kenton's romantic confession to the breaking heart icon.

explainedBy: Though his heart is breaking, Stevens remains totally trapped behind the impenetrable armor of butler decorum.

storyboard.claim: Despite his internal emotional devastation, Stevens cannot break out of his lifelong butler armor.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens bowed beside the protective shield icon, rigidly suppressing any outward confession of agony.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the tragic consequence of Kenton's confession: Stevens' complete inability to respond authentically.
storyboard.addedInformation: Combines the shield icon with Stevens' rigid posture to signify impenetrable emotional repression.

explainedBy: Stevens deflects unbearable intimacy by offering a coldly formal goodbye to Mrs. Benn.

storyboard.claim: Stevens bids farewell to the woman he loves with excruciatingly formal, corporate well-wishes.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens standing with polite, sterile propriety as he delivers his formal farewell to Miss Kenton.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The climactic deflection: Stevens retreats into polite pleasantries instead of embracing her.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the absolute dominance of professional decorum over human longing.

explainedBy: Stevens speaks like a corporate HR manual, lecturing Miss Kenton on retirement as the best part of life.

storyboard.claim: Stevens couches his ultimate farewell in sterile bureaucratic platitudes about retirement and duty.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens reciting platitudes like an HR manager while Miss Kenton looks down in sorrowful resignation.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Analyzes the emotional sterility of Stevens' farewell vocabulary.
storyboard.addedInformation: Exposes how bureaucratic language serves as an emotional defense against genuine feeling.

callout.text: SAY GOODBYE TO THE ONLY WOMAN

explainedBy: Stevens turns away and walks out, saying a formal goodbye to the only woman he has ever loved.

storyboard.claim: Stevens uses detached professional language to walk away forever from the only woman he ever loved.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens turning on his heel and walking away from Miss Kenton, leaving her seated alone at the wet bus station.
storyboard.onScreenText: SAY GOODBYE TO THE ONLY WOMAN
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Executes the physical separation that seals Stevens' permanent romantic exile.
storyboard.addedInformation: Stages Stevens physically departing, abandoning the possibility of romance forever.

explainedBy: Hiding behind formalities at the most critical emotional moment of your life guarantees you will die with regret.

storyboard.claim: Choosing emotional numbness over vulnerability guarantees an unredeemable life of regret.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens standing alone under the heavy coastal sky, bowed under the crushing weight of his irreversible choice.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Summarizes the universal moral lesson of Stevens' tragic parting with Miss Kenton.
storyboard.addedInformation: Translates the specific tragedy of the novel into a universal cautionary truth.

explainedBy: Stevens leaves Miss Kenton, drives his car, and sits down alone on the bench at Weymouth Pier as colored lights turn on.

storyboard.claim: Stevens drives to the seaside town of Weymouth and sits alone on the pier as dusk falls.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens sitting solitary on a wooden pier bench as evening pier illuminations light up overhead.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shifts setting from Little Compton to Weymouth Pier for the book's final scene.
storyboard.addedInformation: Places Stevens alone on the seaside pier bench as festival lights turn on around him.

explainedBy: A friendly stranger sits next to Stevens, notices him weeping, and offers gentle comfort that the evening is the best part of the day.

storyboard.claim: A retired stranger notices Stevens crying on the bench and offers folksy advice about enjoying the evening of life.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens seated on the pier bench weeping quietly while listening to a stranger's warm consoling words.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the pier stranger whose cheerful philosophy gives the book its poignant title metaphor.
storyboard.addedInformation: Captures Stevens' solitary weeping on the public bench amidst evening festive crowds.

explainedBy: Stevens sits with his shattered life and tries desperately to adopt the stranger's cheerful, forward-looking advice.

storyboard.claim: Stevens attempts to adopt the friendly stranger's comforting outlook to keep his despair at bay.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens seated on the bench trying to compose himself and absorb the stranger's advice to rest.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows Stevens grasping for any conceptual lifeline to preserve his emotional composure.
storyboard.addedInformation: Illustrates the pathetic effort of a broken man attempting to adopt casual optimism.

explainedBy: Stevens rationalizes to himself that he should not look back, trying to feel proud of his small contribution to Lord Darlington.

storyboard.claim: Stevens desperately tells himself not to look back and to take pride in serving Lord Darlington.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens in close-up struggling to rebuild his psychological armor of dignified aristocratic service.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Details Stevens' frantic inner rationalization to avoid confronting total moral failure.
storyboard.addedInformation: Exposes the internal mental strain of an old man clinging to a discredited master.

explainedBy: The co-host raises the common critical interpretation that Stevens finds genuine peace and hope at the pier.

storyboard.claim: Some readers view the ending as hopeful, believing Stevens has finally discovered a measure of peace.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens looking thoughtfully toward the sea lights, contemplating whether reconciliation is possible.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Presents the alternative optimistic reading of the novel's final scene.
storyboard.addedInformation: Stages the hopeful interpretation that the following beats will systematically dismantle.

callout.text: ACCEPTING THE EVENING OF HIS LIFE

explainedBy: The host asks if Stevens is finally moving forward by focusing on improving his bantering skills for Mr. Faraday.

storyboard.claim: Is Stevens really moving forward and embracing the evening of his life by practicing witty banter?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens walking along the pier promenade under festive lamps, attempting to practice casual banter.
storyboard.onScreenText: ACCEPTING THE EVENING OF HIS LIFE
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the premise of the hopeful reading to its practical application: bantering.
storyboard.addedInformation: Contrasts the festivity of the pier lamps with Stevens' awkward practice of humor.

explainedBy: The analyst strongly rejects the hopeful interpretation, calling Stevens' ending devastatingly tragic.

storyboard.claim: The ending is not peaceful or hopeful; it is a profoundly devastating portrait of self-deception.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens standing slumped against the pier railing, isolated amidst the festive holidaymakers.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Directly refutes the hopeful interpretation with an uncompromising verdict of tragedy.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strikes through the illusion of peace, revealing the desolate reality of Stevens' condition.

explainedBy: Stevens is not finding peace; he is merely rebooting his defensive denial to avoid confronting catastrophic life waste.

storyboard.claim: Stevens is not discovering serenity; he is rebooting his psychological defense mechanisms to survive despair.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens standing beside the mask icon, rebuilding his emotional facade to avoid total psychological collapse.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the psychological mechanism behind Stevens' sudden enthusiasm for bantering.
storyboard.addedInformation: Uses the mask icon to expose Stevens' newly adopted optimism as another defensive posture.

explainedBy: By deciding his new life's purpose is learning to banter for a new master, Stevens demonstrates he has learned nothing.

storyboard.claim: Surrendering his evening to please yet another master proves Stevens has learned nothing from his wasted life.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A stark close-up of Stevens' impassive, blank expression as he replaces one master's rules with another's.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Delivers the bitter philosophical realization: Stevens remains an unyielding emotional slave.
storyboard.addedInformation: Captures the tragedy of unchanging conformity through a stark blank-faced close-up.

explainedBy: Avoiding emotional reckoning only builds a slightly more modern cage of servitude for Stevens' hollowed soul.

storyboard.claim: Trading classical butler dignity for American bantering merely constructs a modern cage for his repressed soul.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens slumped in sorrow beside the intact chains icon, eternally bound by self-imposed psychological bondage.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Consolidates the indictment of Stevens' final resolution as a new iteration of bondage.
storyboard.addedInformation: Pairs Stevens' defeat with the chains icon to visualize permanent self-imprisonment.

explainedBy: The discussion introduces a major counter-argument: was Stevens merely an innocent victim of the rigid British class system?

storyboard.claim: Critics frequently raise the counterpoint that Stevens was simply a helpless victim of class conditioning.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens positioned in an austere library setting, framed as the subject of socio-cultural analysis.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the critical debate on structural determinism versus personal moral responsibility.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the overarching sociological defense that the next beats will systematically dismantle.

explainedBy: Stevens was born into a rigid hierarchy and raised by a butler father, seemingly lacking any alternative perspective.

storyboard.claim: Born into domestic hierarchy and raised by a strict butler father, Stevens had no progressive liberal education.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens standing in deferential posture, representing generations of unquestioning working-class obedience.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Elaborates the sociological defense of Stevens as an inevitable product of his environment.
storyboard.addedInformation: Emphasizes the generational inheritance of emotional repression passed down from his father.

explainedBy: A refute diagram dismantling the defense that Stevens was a helpless class victim, showing he possessed constant personal agency.

storyboard.claim: Ishiguro systematically disproves the victim narrative by revealing that Stevens possessed continuous moral agency.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A refute diagram striking down the class-victim defense and asserting Stevens' active personal responsibility.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Directly confronts and refutes the deterministic defense articulated in beats 194-195.
storyboard.addedInformation: Replaces sociological fatalism with existential moral culpability via structured refute diagram.

explainedBy: Miss Kenton offered Stevens constant escape routes by bringing fresh flowers into his dark, secluded pantry.

storyboard.claim: Miss Kenton repeatedly offered Stevens opportunities for intimacy, bringing fresh flowers into his dark pantry.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Miss Kenton offering a vase of bright flowers to Stevens, who stands rigid and defensive in his dark pantry.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Demonstrates Stevens' agency through the specific historical moments where he refused human warmth.
storyboard.addedInformation: Stages Miss Kenton offering flowers into Stevens' spartan pantry, symbolizing an offered path to life.

explainedBy: When Miss Kenton held the door to humanity wide open, Stevens deliberately chose cold obedience and shut it in her face.

storyboard.claim: Stevens deliberately rejected intimacy and chose cold obedience because emotional vulnerability terrified him.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens pointing Miss Kenton toward the exit of his pantry, firmly expelling warmth to preserve his walls.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Dramatizes the deliberate refusal of Kenton's affection that cements his moral complicity.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows Stevens actively repelling Miss Kenton's warmth to defend his fortress of solitude.

callout.text: BUILT THE WALLS OF HIS PRISON

explainedBy: Stevens was no helpless victim of aristocracy; he was its willing accomplice who laid every brick of his own emotional prison.

storyboard.claim: Stevens was an active, willing collaborator who deliberately constructed every wall of his personal confinement.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens standing slumped and defeated in the empty hall, realizing he built his own cell brick by brick.
storyboard.onScreenText: BUILT THE WALLS OF HIS PRISON
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Delivers the decisive verdict on Stevens' active complicity in his own emotional ruin.
storyboard.addedInformation: Transforms the metaphor of the class system into a self-constructed architectural prison.

explainedBy: The ultimate tragedy is not what English society stole from Stevens, but the rich emotional life he willingly surrendered.

storyboard.claim: The tragedy of Stevens is not what was taken from him, but the humanity he willingly threw away for false dignity.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens lost in painful self-reflection, confronting the deliberate surrender of his youth and passions.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Clarifies the precise nature of the novel's tragic core: voluntary self-mutilation.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shifts the narrative focus entirely onto Stevens' voluntary abdication of life.

explainedBy: The armor of butler dignity never protected Stevens; it merely blinded him while he served an aristocratic Nazi sympathizer.

storyboard.claim: Professional dignity failed to shield Stevens, serving only to blind him while he facilitated fascist appeasement.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens standing bowed beside the shield motif while Lord Darlington preens in naive aristocratic arrogance.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Exposes the catastrophic political consequence of Stevens' emotional armor.
storyboard.addedInformation: Juxtaposes the shield motif with Lord Darlington's appeasement to show moral blindness.

explainedBy: Butler armor deafened Stevens to true love and ultimately sealed his fate as a living tomb.

storyboard.claim: Repressing his humanity permanently deafened Stevens to love, turning his butler dignity into a spiritual tomb.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens slumped in absolute defeat beside the grave icon, realizing his identity has become his burial vault.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reaches the ultimate metaphor of self-destruction: dignity as a personal sarcophagus.
storyboard.addedInformation: Anchors the grave icon to symbolize the complete spiritual death of Stevens.

explainedBy: The hosts challenge the viewer directly, asking what arbitrary professional rules or frantic schedules they hide behind.

storyboard.claim: The hosts ask the audience what professional facades, rules, or busy schedules they use to hide from reality.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens gesturing outward in a direct address pose, prompting the audience to confront their own evasions.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transitions from the literary analysis of Stevens into a direct modern psychological reflection.
storyboard.addedInformation: Breaks the third-person frame to confront the viewer with their own defensive mechanisms.

explainedBy: Are you using busy careers and professional etiquette to avoid messy conversations and painful moral stands?

storyboard.claim: Do we hide behind professionalism to avoid difficult emotional honesty and uncomfortable moral choices?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens standing in anxious, troubled introspection, embodying the human tendency to evade discomfort.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Deepens the audience self-examination into specific patterns of avoidance.
storyboard.addedInformation: Reflects the universal fear of emotional exposure through Stevens' troubled countenance.

explainedBy: Are we hiding behind professional status to avoid admitting that we are deeply heartbroken?

storyboard.claim: Professional masks are ultimately constructed to avoid the unbearable admission of a broken heart.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A piercing close-up of Stevens' sorrowful eyes, revealing the raw emotional wound behind decades of composure.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pinpoints the deepest layer of defensive avoidance: unadmitted heartbreak.
storyboard.addedInformation: Focuses intimately on Stevens' suppressed sorrow to drive home the emotional toll.

explainedBy: On Weymouth Pier, the sun sets and festive lights turn on, leaving anyone who traded their heart for duty entirely alone.

storyboard.claim: No matter how you ignore your inner life, trading your heart for duty leaves you entirely alone as night falls.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens seated alone on the Weymouth pier bench under festive colored lightbulbs as dusk settles over the sea.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the seaside bench at Weymouth Pier for the ultimate philosophical resolution.
storyboard.addedInformation: Contrasts the bright festival bulbs of the pier with Stevens' profound, solitary isolation.

explainedBy: Stevens sits solitary at dusk, permanently stranded with nothing but the bittersweet remains of his day.

storyboard.claim: In the end, having sacrificed moral freedom and love, you are left entirely alone with the remains of your day.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stevens in quiet close-up at twilight, gazing into the distance with tragic acceptance of his solitary fate.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the video summary on the novel's title motif and final philosophical image.
storyboard.addedInformation: Provides the definitive, poignant closing image of Stevens facing the twilight of his life.
